dimensions: bo 13, length of slide section 2134, bell section entry 17  (total length of both sections 3795, total height of both sections 1495)
provenance: Acquired before 1936 from Hans and Dr. Ulrich Rück
literature: Wörthmüller 1955: 458; Langwill 1974: 57–58, 144; Van der Meer 1979: 94–95, Abb. 150–52 (photos); Fischer 1984: 45; Huber 1989: 357; Waterhouse 1993: 321.
remarks: Only the slide section and bell-stay are by Reichard. Flat slide-stays with dragon-head clasps. Moveable slide-stay has hole, in which a handle for the slide was originally fastened. Bell-stay (by Reichard) engraved: one side has two putti supporting an empty cartouche; on the other side of the bell-stay two lions support a cartouche with Reichard’s master’s mark: “SR,” with a globe below. Adjacent sleeve is nine-sided (nine facets); the individual fields are engraved in two alternating patterns; the same alternating patterns are found on four facets on one side of the sleeves of the slide stays; the other side is round and has engraved head of a soldier wearing a helmet. Ring in slide bow, mounted on leaf-shaped plate with leaf design. Some ferrules are profiled and have one border with punched squares; some have punched squares on both ends with dragon-scale pattern in middle; others have a wreath with punched strokes, pointed tooth pattern and curved arches. According to Huber 1989, the instrument was repaired by Hanns Geyer of Vienna in 1671.
